Context/Background: To find novel treatments and drug combinations that could effectively target colorectal cancer cells (CRCs) and lower the probability of disease relapse, we designed multiple different combinations between cisplatin, cannabidiol (CBD), and intermittent serum starvation (ISS) on colorectal cancer cell lines. We analyzed differentially expressed genes and affected pathways in colorectal cancer cell lines to understand further the potential molecular mechanisms behind the treatments and their interactions.
Prompt: Based on the results of the differential expression analysis of ISS vs DMSO in colorectal cancer cells, run a pathway overrepresentation analysis for statistically significant genes (up and down combined) against the Reactome database. Then, provide a discussion of any relevant affected pathways, highlighting important up and down regulated genes in each.  Focus on any mechanisms by which intermittent serum starvation may alter cancer related pathways.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Differential expression (DE) analysis was performed on colorectal cancer cells treated with intermittent serum starvation (ISS) versus vehicle (DMSO). Using a padj < 0.05 cutoff, 6 555 genes were identified as significantly altered. These DE genes (Ensembl IDs) were mapped to human gene symbols and submitted to an Over-Representation Analysis (ORA) against the Reactome Pathways 2024 library.

Reactome ORA Results (top pathways)  
Term                                     | Overlap | Adj P-value    | Genes (sample)  
----------------------------------------|---------|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------  
Regulation of Cholesterol Biosynthesis by SREBP (SREBF)  
                                         | 42 / 56 | 6.70 × 10⁻⁹   | IDI1; SEC23A; MVK; HMGCR; ACACB; TM7SF2; RXRA; PMVK; SC5D; SCAP; FDFT1; HMGCS1; SREBF1; FDPS; MBTPS1; CREBBP; SREBF2; SQLE; FASN; DHCR7  
Cholesterol Biosynthesis                | 23 / 27 | 1.37 × 10⁻⁶   | IDI1; FDPS; SREBF1; MVK; HMGCS1; CYP51A1; MSMO1; DHCR24; HMGCR; HSD17B7; LSS; ACAT2; SREBF2; TM7SF2; SQLE; EBP; NSDHL; PMVK; SC5D; MVD; DHCR7; LBR; FDFT1  
Membrane Trafficking                    |302 / 633|4.27 × 10⁻¹⁵   | ITSN2; TFRC; KDELR1; GOLGA2; AKT1; AKT2; ULK1; EGFR; RAB11A; SEC31A; NSF; SNX9; ARF1; ARF3; COPA; COPB1; DESTINATIONS…  
ER to Golgi Anterograde Transport       | 87 / 155|2.85 × 10⁻⁸   | ARF1; ARF3; KDELR1; MIA3; GOLGA2; COPA; COPB1; SEC13; TMED3; TMED7; TMED9; NSF; GOSR1; GOSR2; SAR1B; ARCN1; DYNLL1; DYNLL2; …  
TP53 Regulates Transcription of Additional Cell Cycle Genes With Uncertain Roles  
                                         | 17 / 21 |1.93 × 10⁻⁴   | TP53; PLK2; PLK3; BTG2; CDC25C; CNOT1; CNOT2; CNOT3; CNOT4; CNOT6L; CNOT7; CNOT8; CNOT10; CNOT11; RGCC; TNKS1BP1; CNOT …  
ATF6 (ATF6-alpha) Activates Chaperones  | 10 / 12 |6.46 × 10⁻³   | ATF6; XBP1; HSPA5; HSP90B1; CALR; DDIT3; MBTPS1; MBTPS2; NFYA; NFYB  

Discussion  
1. Lipid metabolism—particularly cholesterol biosynthesis—emerged as the most overrepresented module. Key regulators SREBF1/2, HMGCR and HMGCS1 (rate-limiting enzymes of the mevalonate pathway) and downstream enzymes (FDPS, MVK, FDFT1, SQLE, DHCR7) were among the DE set, implicating ISS in rewiring membrane lipid synthesis.  
2. The “Regulation of Cholesterol Biosynthesis by SREBP” pathway (Adj P = 6.7 × 10⁻⁹) suggests altered SREBP-mediated transcriptional control under nutrient stress, potentially reducing lipid availability for proliferating CRC cells.  
3. Enrichment of TP53-regulated cell-cycle genes (e.g., TP53 itself, CDC25C, BTG2, PLK2/3, RGCC) points to enhanced p53-dependant checkpoints or stress responses triggered by serum withdrawal.  
4. Activation of ER stress/unfolded-protein-response nodes (ATF6→HSPA5, XBP1, DDIT3) indicates ISS imposes proteostatic stress, which may synergize with chemotherapy to induce CRC cell death.  
5. Broad enrichment of membrane-trafficking and ER→Golgi transport factors (ARF1/3, COPA/B1, SEC proteins, NSF) suggests continuing secretory flow despite nutrient limitation, potentially as an adaptive reorganization of receptor trafficking (e.g., EGFR) in response to ISS.

Mechanistic insight: intermittent serum starvation in CRC cells likely imposes two major stresses—metabolic stress (via down-tuning cholesterol and fatty-acid synthesis through SREBP axes) and proteostatic stress (via ATF6/XBP1 chaperone activation). Concurrent activation of p53 targets may enforce cell-cycle arrest, amplifying starvation-induced cytostasis. Altered membrane trafficking may also modulate growth-factor receptor dynamics under low-nutrient conditions.
